title: [Audit] 🚨 Security & Anomalies
description: Mean-severity risk scoring, privileged operations, failures and newly seen identities.

config.description: Average severity weight across scoring events, on the same 0–50 scale as the weights: config change 50, key invalidation 45, failure 40, anonymous denial 35, destructive change 30, other Kibana change 25, workflow execution 10. Executions weigh least on purpose — they are the one class with unbounded cadence, and a scheduled workflow firing every minute would otherwise turn total risk back into an event count. Routine activity scores 0 and is excluded, so this is not a disguised event count — read it with Scoring events beside it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("invalidate_apikeys","anonymous_access_denied") OR (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.event.action, scc = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, attributes.event.outcome, resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ",") | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | STATS risk_total = SUM(risk * n), scoring_events = SUM(n) | EVAL mean_severity = ROUND(1.0 * risk_total / scoring_events, 1) | EVAL `Mean severity (of 50)` = mean_severity | KEEP `Mean severity (of 50)`

config.title: 🚨 Security configuration changes
config.description: Raw security_config_change payloads, grouped by identity and action. The field is a JSON string, shown verbatim — it names the exact API key ids or profile uids affected. A long payload (an invalidation listing many keys) is cut at the column edge; the Config-change event feed below shows each one in full. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_change = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, action = attributes.event.action, change = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change | SORT last_change DESC | LIMIT 12

config.title: Rare and privileged operations
config.description: The highest-severity scoring actions in range, one row per action and weight, placed by how often each happened: rarer is further left, so the top-left is rare and high-severity — look there first. Colour is the severity weight. A failed change scores 40 whatever it changed, so it gets its own row, marked (failed). Hover a point for how many identities did it and when. Routine activity scores 0 and is not shown.

config.title: Risk over time
config.description: Summed severity weight per interval, routine activity excluded, split by who it came from: tenant identities, Elastic platform automation, or unauthenticated requests. Spikes are clusters of privileged, failed or denied activity.

config.title: Identities by first appearance in range
config.description: Identities ordered by their first event inside the selected range, latest first. First seen is within the range, not ever: an identity that was already active when the range opened also shows a first-seen near its start. New in range reads "no" for those (first seen in the opening twelfth of the range). A "yes" near the top is an identity worth a question; widen the range to tell a new identity from a returning one. Client IPs is 0 for identities whose events record no client address (the Kibana service account, platform automation). An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY actor | SORT first_seen DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | EVAL new_in_range = CASE(TO_LONG(first_seen) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart)) > (TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart))) / 12, "yes", "no") | LIMIT 10

config.title: Risk leaderboard
config.description: Identities ranked by total accumulated severity, so sustained behaviour outranks a single high-severity event. Scope separates tenant identities from Elastic platform automation and unauthenticated requests — without it elastic.maintenance can top this table, because Elastic platform automation performs routine security config changes itself. API keys and native users carry no email; click an email, where there is one, to pin that identity across the whole suite. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.

config.title: Why these identities scored — every risky action, with its weight
config.description: The receipts behind the leaderboard: for each identity, exactly which actions scored, what each one weighed, how many times, and when it last happened. Risk total is weight × events, the same quantity the leaderboard sums. This is what turns a score into evidence. Click an email to pin that identity across the suite. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.

config.title: Failures and denials by identity
config.description: Failed and denied operations grouped by identity, action and source IP. Scope separates unauthenticated probes from tenant identities and Elastic platform automation. API keys and native users (elastic, admin) carry no email, so an empty email does not mean an external probe — read Scope. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, attributes.user.email, action = attributes.event.action, ip = client.ip | SORT events DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | LIMIT 8
